messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up from the RFC — sketching operational patterns for deferred-ack + resume tokens on streaming requests. TL;DR proposal: server can early-ack with a stream-id header, we allow midstream resume with token+offset, and retries require explicit idempotency/dedupe. High level thoughts?

jon: I like the early-ack idea for admission control. Means gateway can admit and quota quickly while runtime drives the stream. But need to be careful about client-visible latencies for first-data. :thinking:

maria: two quick constraints: (1) legacy clients -> must still support plain long-polling without resume tokens, (2) resume tokens add state in the proxy if tokens are opaque pointers. We should prefer stateless tokens if possible.

elaine: agreed on stateless tokens preference. Proposal: token = base64(hmac(stream-id | offset | expiry)) so edge can validate without DB. Small state for in-flight window only.

sam: risk: if token includes offset, what about partial responses that are non-idempotent (side-effects)? We should only allow resume for read-only/generative calls. For calls that mutate downstream, require strong dedupe-id or full single-shot mode.

nora: +1. Also: if we early-ack with 202 + Stream-ID, show clients this header so they can reconnect: `X-RW-Stream-ID: s_abcdef123` and `Retry-Policy: resume-v1`. Example:

```http
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
X-RW-Stream-ID: s_abcdef123
X-RW-Resume-Token: eyJvZmZzIjoxMjMsInR5cGUiOiJ2MSJ9...
Content-Type: application/json

{ "status": "accepted" }
```

jon: Good. How about cancellations? If client sends CANCEL midstream, gateway should forward abort downstream and mark resume token invalid. But if upstream keeps producing (slowly), we need an eviction TTL so runtime can GC.

maria: eviction TTL needs to be tunable per customer tier. Dedicated customers can opt for longer resume windows. We should expose `resume_ttl` in the route config.

elaine: Implementation tradeoffs: option A) gateway validates stateless token and proxies directly to runtime where runtime replays from offset; option B) gateway keeps small ring-buffer for each admitted stream and can replay short windows without runtime involvement. Which do we prefer?

sam: Option B reduces load on runtime for short disconnects but increases memory complexity on gateway. I think keep it optional: `edge.replay_buffer_bytes` default 0, opt-in per route.

nora: Edge replay buffer also helps with network flakiness on mobile. We can prioritize small buffers (e.g., 64KB) and require `dedupe-id` for anything > 0.

maria: Observability: we must include metrics: stream_admits, stream_resumes, resume_miss, replay_buffer_hit, resume_expired. Add tracing tags: `rw.stream.id`, `rw.resume.offset`, `rw.resume.result=(hit|miss|invalid)`.

jon: On retry semantics: client retries should only be attempted against gateway if resume token present OR request marked `idempotency-key`. Otherwise client should surface error to app layer. Add HTTP response code 409 for resume invalid so clients can surface a clear path.

elaine: I'll draft a small spec with config knobs, header names, and example flows. Next steps: assign owners for (a) token format + HMAC spec, (b) gateway replay buffer prototype, (c) client SDK changes. @sam @maria volunteer? :thumbsup:

sam: I can take token format + SDK docs.

maria: I'll own the gateway buffer prototype (small PoC) and metrics.

infra-bot: Deployment note: will require new feature flag `edge.resume_tokens_enabled` and canary rollout.

elaine: thanks — I'll post the mini-spec in the RFC thread and link the prototype PR when ready.

jon: quick nit: add an anti-abuse TTL on tokens (max 24h) even for enterprise. Also consider rate-limiting resume attempts to avoid brute-force reconnections.

maria: noted. I'll include rate-limit buckets per stream-id and resum e-try counters.

elaine: cool — closing this thread, moving spec to RFC follow-up doc. If anyone has more edge cases (s3-style multipart-like replays, or function-calls with side effects) drop them here before EOD. Thanks! :rocket!
